text: Every flow you've built so far has run top to bottom, in a single straight line — trigger, then Step 1, then Step 2, then Step 3. Real business processes aren't straight lines. Flow Designer's native If/Else lets a flow branch into one of two paths, and it does it with no scripting at all.

The condition itself uses a pattern you already know from elsewhere in this platform: field, operator, value — the exact same structure behind an ACL condition and a list filter. Priority is Critical. Cost is greater than one thousand. Multiple conditions can be combined with AND or OR, just like a list filter's condition builder.

Once the condition is in place, Flow Designer gives you two branches right on the canvas. The If branch runs its own sequence of actions only when the condition evaluates true. The Else branch runs a separate sequence only when it evaluates false. The flow evaluates the condition exactly once per execution and commits to a single path.

Take an Incident Created trigger as a real example. The condition checks whether the incident's Priority field equals Critical. If that's true, the If branch sends an urgent SMS notification straight to the on-call engineer. If it's false, the Else branch sends a standard email notification to the assignment group instead.

Before Flow Designer existed, this kind of branching logic lived inside a Business Rule, written as an actual if statement in server-side JavaScript — work that required a developer. Now an administrator builds the same decision-making power visually, right inside the flow's canvas, where anyone maintaining the process later can read it at a glance.
One condition, two branches, zero lines of code. Next up: looping that same kind of logic over every single item in a list, using Flow Designer's For Each construct.
